full_text_en:
Hu Shaokun Bribery Case

Defendant: Hu Shaokun, male, 26 years old, formerly a staff member of the Wenjindu Sub-office of Kowloon Customs. He was arrested on February 9, 1988.

The case of defendant Hu Shaokun for bribery was instituted as a public prosecution by the People's Procuratorate of Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province, to the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court. The court formed a collegial panel according to law, and after public trial found the following facts:

From March 1987, the defendant Hu Shaokun and Hong Kong smuggler Wu Qingquan (dealt with in a separate case) engaged in multiple secret conspiracies, agreeing that Hu Shaokun would conduct fake verification cancellation for Wu Qingquan and Hong Kong merchants in smuggling activities to evade customs supervision, and accept bribes in return. Thereafter, Wu Qingquan had someone privately engrave the seal of Wenjindu Customs for reviewing import and export goods declarations, and contacted cargo owners to collect the "Registration Manual for Import and Export Goods of Processing and Assembly and Small and Medium-sized Compensation Trade" (hereinafter referred to as "Registration Manual") and the "Customs Declaration Form for Export Goods of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as "Declaration Form"). After Wu Qingquan filled in the export date, transport vehicle license plate number, and affixed the privately engraved review seal on the Registration Manual and Declaration Form that had already been filled in by the cargo owner with items such as goods name, specifications, quantity, value, etc., he handed over the Declaration Form to Hu Shaokun as agreed. Hu Shaokun took advantage of his convenience as a staff member at Wenjindu Customs to mix the fake Declaration Forms into the export goods declaration forms to be sent to various customs offices for verification cancellation, and sent them to various places for counterfeit verification cancellation. From March to August 1987, Hu Shaokun placed fake declaration forms more than 10 times, totaling 232 sheets, and through this counterfeit verification cancellation, he processed over 2,544,000 yards of nylon cloth, over 800,000 yards of lining cloth, 325 tons of zippers, and over 45,000 copies of calendars. The total value of the goods processed through counterfeit verification cancellation was over RMB 20,690,000. Each time after placing the fake forms, Hu Shaokun would settle the bribes he should receive with Wu Qingquan. Over nearly half a year, Hu Shaokun accepted a total of HKD 908,000 and RMB 464,405.92 (including the value of one gold necklace and one gold bracelet converted into cash). In September and October 1987, after some of the fake declaration forms placed by Hu Shaokun were discovered by customs in Quanzhou, Fujian Province, and Shantou, Guangdong Province, Wu Qingquan demanded back HKD 330,000 in bribe money from Hu Shaokun. Hu Shaokun actually received bribes totaling approximately RMB 464,400 and HKD 578,000.

After accepting bribes, the defendant Hu Shaokun hid the illicit money and goods in a brown combination lock suitcase at his uncle's home. When the case was exposed on January 29, 1988, Hu Shaokun absconded. On February 6, 1988, Hu Shaokun was captured. Subsequently, the Shenzhen People's Procuratorate seized the combination lock suitcase along with the illicit money and goods.

The above criminal facts of defendant Hu Shaokun are proved by collected physical evidence, expert conclusions, witness testimony, and documentary evidence, and Hu Shaokun also confessed to them without reservation. The facts are fully established.

The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court held: The defendant Hu Shaokun, being a customs staff member, used his official position to provide fake declaration form verification cancellation for illegal Hong Kong merchants smuggling goods, and accepted bribes in return. His conduct constituted the crime of bribery under Article 185 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. In accordance with the provisions of Article 1(2) of the "Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Regarding the Severe Punishment of Criminals Who Seriously Sabotage the Economy," and by analogy with the crime of embezzlement under Article 155 of the Criminal Law, he should be punished. The amount of bribes accepted by Hu Shaokun was especially huge, the circumstances of the crime were especially serious, the nature was especially vile, and it caused serious losses to state interests, so he should be severely punished. According to the facts and circumstances of Hu Shaokun's crime, in accordance with Article 53(1) of the Criminal Law, he should be deprived of political rights for life. In accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law, all property obtained illegally by Hu Shaokun shall be recovered. Accordingly, on February 4, 1990, the court rendered judgment as follows:

1. The defendant Hu Shaokun is guilty of the crime of bribery and is sentenced to death, with deprivation of political rights for life.
2. The property obtained illegally by the defendant Hu Shaokun that has been seized shall be recovered and turned over to the state treasury.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, defendant Hu Shaokun appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court.

The Guangdong High People's Court on second instance held: Hu Shaokun's grounds for appeal were untenable. After discussion and decision by its judicial committee, in accordance with Article 136(1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on March 28, 1990, it rendered a ruling to reject the appeal of appellant Hu Shaokun and sustain the original judgment. It also, in accordance with Article 145(2) of the Criminal Procedure Law, submitted a request to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

The Supreme People's Court, in accordance with the death penalty review procedure of the Criminal Procedure Law, reviewed the case and held: The first-instance judgment and second-instance ruling found the facts of Hu Shaokun's crime clear, the evidence reliable and sufficient, the conviction accurate, the sentencing appropriate, and the trial procedure lawful. On April 26, 1990, it approved the criminal ruling of the Guangdong High People's Court sustaining the original judgment sentencing Hu Shaokun to death for the crime of bribery with deprivation of political rights for life.
